title: Watchlists: Persistent Entity Tracking
content:
Watchlists are named collections of entities you want to monitor over time. Each watchlist has a type that determines what kind of entities it tracks and which sidecar endpoints are queried when checking for new activity.

Supported entity types: ip (IP addresses checked against threat intel feeds), ticker (stock symbols checked against market data), region (geographic areas checked against conflict and weather data), cve (CVE IDs checked against vulnerability databases), vessel (MMSI numbers or vessel names checked against AIS data), callsign (aircraft callsigns checked against ADS-B data).

Lifecycle: Create a watchlist with watchlist_manage({ action: "create", name: "my-list", type: "ip", items: ["1.2.3.4"] }). Add or remove items later with add_items and remove_items actions. Check for new activity with watchlist_check({ name: "my-list" }) — this queries live data and returns only items with changes since the last check. The last-checked timestamp updates automatically.

Storage: Watchlists persist to the MCP server's data directory as JSON files under the watchlists/ subdirectory. They survive server restarts and are available across sessions.

Best practices: Keep watchlists focused — one per investigation or theme. Use descriptive names like "ukraine-ips" or "energy-tickers". Check watchlists periodically or let the sentinel scheduler handle automated checks. Review and prune stale watchlists regularly with the list and delete actions.
